clue.text: A card he changed in game for pretentious players

definitions.note: in this parlour game the players pretend, acting out words in mime

indicators.note: the letters of these three words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone swaps a card during a game played by show-offs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the letters of A CARD HE. The definition is playful: players of this game act and pretend, so they are 'pretentious' in a literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A guessing game in which teams mime syllables of a word is played by people putting on an act.

clue.text: Record a little boy's held, by gum!

indicators.note: the boy's name is held within the word for gum

parts.note: chicle is the gum of the sapodilla tree used for chewing gum
Ron is a short boy's name, a little form of Ronald

explanation.surface: An exclamation at hearing a small child is being detained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by gum!' looks like a mild oath but supplies CHICLE, chewing-gum base.
explanation.definitionFit: A history set down in order of time is a written account of events.

clue.text: A female relation with a message that's friendly

parts.note: relation here means a story told; one with a moral is a fable

explanation.surface: A woman relative bearing news is pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' suggests a family member; here it means a narration, and one with a moral is a FABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An amiable person is easy to talk to and good-natured.

clue.text: Improving rider has a mount — tip to people entering

indicators.note: the tip and people go into the abbreviated mount

parts.note: Mt is the abbreviation for mount, a mountain
a tip is an end
men are people

explanation.surface: A horseman gets better by acquiring a horse and advice for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rider' suggests a horseman but is a clause added to a bill; 'mount' is not a horse but MT. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause added to a bill or contract to change it for the better is a rider.

clue.text: Play poor shot and get boundary

explanation.surface: A batsman plays a bad stroke yet still scores four.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket to edge is to hit the ball off the bat's edge, a poor shot; and an edge is a border.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket miscue off the side of the bat, and the outer limit or border of something.

clue.text: Facts about top people from TV doctor's medical group

parts.note: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC television time traveller, and 's stands for 'is'
WHO is the World Health Organization, a United Nations health body

explanation.surface: Gossip about celebrities leaked from a television doctor's practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The reference book of this name lists biographical details of eminent people.
explanation.definitionFit: The reference book of this title gives biographical details of prominent living people.

clue.text: 7 criticising festive performance

parts.note: the answer to 7 down is the element whose chemical symbol is W
assailing someone is attacking them with criticism

explanation.surface: An element criticises a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' means the answer to 7 down, WOLFRAM (tungsten), whose symbol is W. Wassailing is going from house to house singing and drinking at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol singing door to door at Christmas, with toasts of spiced ale, is a seasonal entertainment.

clue.text: A cone may appear when it's stormy

definitions.text: A cone may appear when it's stormy

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning cone is hoisted at sea when the weather turns rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it's stormy' rearranges A CONE; storm cones were hoisted at coastguard stations as gale warnings, and the whole clue describes the sea in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The open sea is where storm-cone warnings matter and where a rough tempest shows itself.

clue.text: Animals often after ewes? It's elementary

parts.note: a wolf hunts sheep, and a ram pursues ewes to mate, so both animals are after ewes
a wolf hunts sheep, and a ram pursues ewes to mate, so both animals are after ewes

explanation.surface: Animals tend to chase female sheep: obvious!
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives two animals that each go after ewes for different reasons. 'It's elementary' sounds like 'obvious' but means a chemical element: wolfram is tungsten.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten, also called by this name, is a chemical element.

clue.text: Had a row with second in command, a leftist

indicators.note: only the second letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: a red is a communist, a political leftist

explanation.surface: Someone quarrelled with the deputy officer, a socialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second in command' looks like a deputy but gives only O, the second letter of COMMAND. 'Had a row' means rowed a boat, not quarrelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To have propelled a boat with oars is to have rowed it.

clue.text: Weapon left in general's keeping

indicators.note: the general's word holds and keeps the other letter inside it

parts.note: general in the sense of widespread or prevalent gives rife

explanation.surface: A gun left in the custody of an army general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like the army officer, but it is the adjective meaning widespread, RIFE, which keeps L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled firearm fired from the shoulder is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Good newsreader?

parts.note: the Gospel means 'good news', so its reader in church is a reader of good news, not a television presenter

explanation.walkthrough: Gospel comes from Old English 'god spel', good news; the clue pretends to praise a TV announcer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric who reads the Gospel aloud at a service is reading out the good news of the scriptures.

clue.text: Diarist's critical comment on wine

explanation.surface: A diary writer records a harsh verdict on a wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody is a comic Victorian novel by George and Weedon Grossmith, kept by Charles Pooter. A wine with no body is thin, so the phrase is a wine critic's put-down. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooter, the comic diarist, is the insignificant person of the book's title; and a thin wine is said to lack fullness of flavour.

clue.text: Artificial rouge married girl has on

indicators.note: the married girl is placed on, that is before, the colour in this across answer

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
rouge is French for red

explanation.surface: A wedded young woman wears red make-up to look affected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rouge' suggests make-up but is simply the French word for red, RED, which comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannered style is affected and stilted, so it seems contrived rather than natural.

clue.text: Bar American bowler in closely contested match

parts.note: a local is a British pub near one's home
in the US a bowler hat is called a derby

explanation.surface: A US cricket bowler refused entry to a tight game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket but is the hat. A local derby is a game between neighbouring teams, usually fiercely fought.
explanation.definitionFit: A game between neighbouring rival teams is typically fought hard by both sides.

clue.text: West Indians outside railway, junction

indicators.note: the Indian people are placed outside, around, the letter for West

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada

explanation.surface: Caribbean cricketers wait outside a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Indians' reads as one phrase but splits into W and CREE. CREWE is a town in Cheshire, England, famous as a major railway junction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheshire town grew up around the meeting point of several main lines, the best-known rail interchange in England.

clue.text: Part of this statesman's address is OK

definitions.text: Part of this statesman's address is OK

parts.words: Part of this statesman's address is OK
parts.note: read statesman as state's man: a man from the state whose postal abbreviation, in his address, is OK

explanation.walkthrough: 'statesman' suggests a politician; it is a man from a state. US postal addresses use the two-letter code OK for Oklahoma.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of the US state abbreviated OK on envelopes is a native of that state, a state's man.

clue.text: Feeling giddy? This helps one see where one's going

definitions.text: This helps one see where one's going

explanation.surface: A dizzy person asks for something to light the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, head light is a light head, feeling dizzy; and a car's front lamp lights the road ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-headedness means dizziness, and a vehicle's front lamp illuminates the road ahead.

clue.text: Extra special delivery for magazine

parts.note: something extra is fresh or additional, hence new
a yorker is a cricket delivery pitched at the batsman's feet

explanation.surface: An urgent postal service is laid on for a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special delivery' suggests the post; in cricket a yorker is a ball bowled to land at the batter's toes. The New Yorker is a US weekly magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Yorker is a well-known American weekly periodical.

clue.text: Regards series as something unpleasant for viewers

parts.note: to regard is to look at, so regards means eyes, as in eyes up
a train is a series or sequence, as in a train of events

explanation.surface: Someone considers a television series to be a nasty experience for its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' sounds like a TV audience but means anyone using their eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching eyes from too much reading or screen time are a discomfort suffered by people who look.

clue.text: One sort of slip another might correct

definitions.text: One sort of slip another might correct

parts.words: One sort of slip another might correct
parts.note: one kind of slip, a printed paper slip, corrects another kind, a slip of the pen

explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' is used twice in different senses: a mistake, and a slip of paper listing corrections.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed correction note inserted in a book fixes an error, which is itself a slip.

clue.text: Shining silver base

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
base means low or mean in character

explanation.surface: A gleaming metal base for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silver base' suggests a metal stand; it gives AG plus LOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glowing is bright and radiant, giving off light.

clue.text: Needy person, we hear, in Japan

indicators.note: the word is as it is heard, said aloud

parts.note: someone who lacks things is a lacker

explanation.surface: A poor person, rumour has it, is in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' looks like the country, but japan is also a hard black varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a glossy black varnish, a kind of hard shiny coating for wood or metal.

clue.text: The home, so to speak, in which female and I live

parts.note: to live somewhere is to reside there

explanation.surface: A man describes the house he shares with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' signals the figurative sense: the hearth stands for home life.
explanation.definitionFit: The area round the hearth is a figure for domestic life, as in fireside chats.

clue.text: From clues, odd bits come to centre of attention

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on, are taken

explanation.surface: Picking out the odd parts of the clues gets you the main point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits' picks letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of FROM CLUES.
explanation.definitionFit: A focal point is where interest and attention converge.

clue.text: Investment in antique furniture

explanation.surface: Putting money into old furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' suggests finance; militarily, to invest a town is to besiege it. Siege is also an archaic word for a seat, as in the Siege Perilous of Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrounding a fortress is a blockade; and the old word for a seat or throne.

clue.text: Smart chap has to appear after furious female

parts.note: a smart alec is a know-all, so the chap's name is Alec
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever man has to turn up after an angry woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Alecto is one of the three Furies, so 'furious female' is literal. 'has' and 'appear after' simply link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: She is one of the Erinyes, the avenging goddesses of Greek myth, so a Fury is literally a furious woman.

clue.text: Weight precisely stated for fruit

indicators.note: the word is stated, spoken aloud

parts.note: a plumb is a lead weight, and plumb also means exactly, as in plumb in the middle

explanation.surface: Someone states a weight exactly for some produce.
explanation.walkthrough: One word covers both 'Weight' and 'precisely': plumb, the bob on a line, and the adverb meaning exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum is a sweet stone fruit.

clue.text: Wells, for example, in which you'll find most of treacle had collected

indicators.note: the letters are collected together and reassembled in a new order
the final letter of treacle is dropped, leaving most of the word

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the spa town, treacle had pooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims TREACLE to TREACL; 'collected' rearranges TREACL plus HAD. Wells, in Somerset, England, is a small city with a famous cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somerset city of Wells is known for its great medieval church, the seat of a bishop.

clue.text: Composer's first bit of good fortune

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: fortune here means luck, good or bad

explanation.surface: A composer's first stroke of good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Christoph Willibald Gluck was an 18th-century German opera composer. The 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluck wrote the opera Orfeo ed Euridice, so he is an example of a writer of music.

clue.text: Brief pronouncement's typically warm

indicators.note: the pronounced form of the synonym for brief is what is wanted

parts.note: a brief is a short account, a summary

explanation.surface: A short statement is usually friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' is the noun, an outline; said aloud it gives the word for hot-season weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather like that of the hottest season is characteristically sunny and hot.

clue.text: More grown up, turning 19

indicators.note: the letters of the other answer are turned about into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 19 down, a slip correcting an error

explanation.surface: A child grows older as their birthday approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' means the answer to 19 down, ERRATUM, whose letters 'turning' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning adult or fully developed, so older and wiser.
